The AI Listing Agent is the core intelligence system that transforms raw product data into marketplace-optimized product listings.
The AI Listing Agent orchestrates multiple specialized sub-agents.
The AI Listing Agent manages context assembly.
The AI Listing Agent handles structured output validation.
The AI Listing Agent implements bounded correction loops.
The Listing Agent receives a rich context object assembled from multiple data sources.
Product Data is raw product information from import.

Agent input Marketplace Context: Amazon rules.
Agent input Marketplace Context: Flipkart rules.

Architecture Diagram: AI Listing Agent Internal Pipeline
Pipeline node INPUT: Agent Input: Product + Brand + Rules + Category.
Pipeline node RET: Brand Voice Retriever - pgvector.
Pipeline node ORCH: Agent Orchestrator - LangGraph.
Parallel Agent Execution includes CA: Content Agent.
Parallel Agent Execution includes KA: Keyword Agent.
Parallel Agent Execution includes AA: Attribute Agent.
Parallel Agent Execution includes IA: Image Agent.
Pipeline node JSON: Canonical Listing JSON.
Pipeline node CORR: Correction Loop - max 3.
INPUT --> CTX (Agent Input to Context Builder).
CTX --> RET (Context Builder to Brand Voice Retriever).
RET --> PB (Brand Voice Retriever to Prompt Builder).
PB --> ORCH (Prompt Builder to Agent Orchestrator).
ORCH --> PARALLEL (Orchestrator to Parallel Agent Execution).
PARALLEL --> MERGE (parallel agents to Output Merger).
MERGE --> JSON (Output Merger to Canonical Listing JSON).
JSON --> VAL (Canonical Listing JSON to Validation Pipeline).
VAL -->|PASS| APPROVE (validation pass goes to Human Approval).
VAL -->|FAIL| CORR (validation fail goes to Correction Loop).
CORR --> VAL (Correction Loop returns to Validation Pipeline).
APPROVE --> EXEC (Human Approval to Marketplace Execution).
The Listing Agent produces a canonical listing JSON.
Canonical listing output: Title — Marketplace-optimized product title.
Canonical listing output: Bullets — Key feature bullet points.
Canonical listing output: Description — Rich product description.
Canonical listing output: Keywords — search terms.
Canonical listing output: Keywords — backend keywords.
Canonical listing output: Attributes — structured attributes matching category schema.
Canonical listing output: ImageReports — compliance status per image per slot.
Canonical listing output Metadata: model used.
ListingAgent orchestrates the complete listing generation pipeline.
async def generate(self, product_id: str, marketplace: str) -> ListingResult.
Step 1: build context via await self.context_builder.build(product_id, marketplace).
Step 2: retrieve brand voice chunks via brand_chunks = await self.retriever.retrieve(...).
Retrieved chunks are set on context.brand_chunks.
Step 3: build prompts for each sub-agent via self.prompt_builder.build(context).
Step 4: execute agent graph (parallel agents + validation + correction) via result = await self.orchestrator.execute(context, prompts).
generate returns result, the output of self.orchestrator.execute(context, prompts), as its ListingResult.
Listing Agent outputs: Canonical Listing JSON with metadata.
Invariant: All output passes through Rules Engine.
Invariant: Brand voice retrieval uses cosine similarity.
Listing Agent must never bypass validation.
Listing Agent must never publish directly.
Listing Agent must never use hardcoded model names.
Listing Agent must never ignore brand context.
Listing Agent must never generate without marketplace rules loaded.
Description: covers graph state, nodes, edges, conditional routing, retry nodes, and human approval interrupt (itemised below).
Keywords: orchestration, LangGraph, graph, nodes, edges, state, parallel, conditional
LangGraph provides the orchestration framework for the AI Listing Agent.
The generation pipeline is modelled as a directed graph.
Graph-based orchestration: complex agent workflows modelled as nodes and edges.
Typed state: AgentState is a structured object that flows through the graph.
Conditional routing: branch based on validation results.
Conditional routing: branch based on retry counts.
Conditional routing: branch based on error types.
Human-in-the-loop: interrupt the graph at the approval node.
Human-in-the-loop: resume the graph after human decision.
Persistence: state can be resumed after interrupts.
Persistence: state can be resumed after failures.
Parallel execution: multiple nodes can execute concurrently via branching edges.
Transient AgentState field: brand_context (re-retrieved on resume).
Table header: Node | Purpose | Input | Output
Node retrieve_brand: pgvector cosine similarity retrieval.
Node attribute_agent: map product to category schema.
Node merge_outputs: combine all agent outputs.
Node correct: fix specific fields based on errors.
Node publish: send to marketplace adapter.
Architecture Diagram: LangGraph Agent Execution Graph
content_agent (node CA) runs in Parallel Agents.
keyword_agent (node KA) runs in Parallel Agents.
attribute_agent (node AA) runs in Parallel Agents.
image_agent (node IA) runs in Parallel Agents.
CHECK passed? No --> decision node RETRY_CHECK "retry_count < 3?".
RETRY_CHECK retry_count < 3? No --> node BLOCKED labelled "job_blocked".
When the graph reaches the await_approval node, execution pauses.
When the graph reaches await_approval, the state is persisted.
When the human approves or rejects, the graph resumes from the checkpoint.
Checkpointing enables long-lived workflows that span hours or days of human review.
Checkpointing enables recovery from server restarts during execution.
Checkpointing enables an audit trail of every state transition.
